## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Background
• The Utah Assessment and Accountability Directors
 (assessment and accountability specialists in Utah school
 districts) sent a request to USBE to have the state switch from
 a cohort-referenced to a baseline-referenced SGP model.
• We want to consider the opportunities and tradeoffs
 associated with their request.

 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 2</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">According to UAAD….
• The Advantages of a Baseline-Referenced Model Are:
 ▪ Immediate Results: Growth calculations can be performed
 immediately following assessments, allowing data to inform
 instructional and programmatic decisions promptly…
 ▪ Stable and Consistent Comparison: Schools will have stable
 reference points across years, allowing clearer longitudinal
 analysis…
 ▪ Enhanced Utility for Planning: Immediate availability of actionable
 data supports timely and strategic school improvement efforts...
• We will examine these and other claims.

 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 3</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Growth Percentiles
• SGPs describe the relative location of a
 student’s current score compared to
 the current scores of students with
 similar score histories.
• The location in this reference group of
 “academic peers” is expressed as a
 percentile rank. For example, a student
 earning an SGP of 80 performed as well
 as or better than 80 percent of her Norm- and Criterion-Referenced Student
 academic peers. Growth (2009)
 D. Betebenner
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 5</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGPs and Key Questions from Castellano &amp; Ho
1. What primary interpretation is best supported?
 ▪ Growth description—SGPs describe the relative performance of students by
 comparing their current scores to those of a set of students with similar scores
 on prior grade-level tests. The SGP metric expresses this relative status in
 terms of percentile ranks.
 ▪ Growth projection—The SGP model is easily extended to describe the growth
 necessary for students to reach important milestones (e.g., proficient, CCR).
2. What is the statistical foundation of the model?
 ▪ SGPs are calculated using quantile regression, which is a non-parametric
 regression approach that can better fit non-linear data, especially for high and
 low performers.
3. What are the required data features?
 ▪ SGPs require at least 5,000 students per grade/content area, which is
 not a problem with any state. At least one prior score is required, but
 two prior scores improves the accuracy substantially.
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 7</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGPs and Key Questions from Castellano &amp; Ho
4. What kinds of group-level interpretations are best supported?
 ▪ SGPs are easily aggregated at the subgroup, school, district, and state levels using
 medians or means. Medians describe the typical growth at the aggregate level,
 while means describe the average growth.
5. Does the model set standards for expected or adequate growth?
 ▪ The 50th percentile is implicitly defined as typical growth, but some type of
 standard-setting approach is necessary to define high, typical, low, and any other
 level of growth (see next slide).
6. What are the common misinterpretations and unintended
 consequences?
 ▪ Student Growth Percentiles are often incorrectly assumed to describe an absolute
 amount of growth, but they are normative because “growth” is determined with
 respect to other students in the model with a similar score history.
 ▪ As intuitive as SGPs seem to be, we often find confusion with things like percent
 correct.
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 8</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Types of SGPs
• Cohort-referenced SGPs: These are the typical SGPs that are normed
 within each year such that the median SGP for each grade/content
 area = 50 at the state level.
• Adequate Growth Percentiles (AGPs) represent the growth students
 must make (in a percentile metric) each year to reach a specific score/
 achievement target (e.g., proficiency) in a specified amount of time.
• Baseline-referenced SGPs: Unlike coherent-referenced SGPs, baseline-
 referenced SGPs evaluate current growth against some baseline group
 (e.g., student growth between 2018 and 2019). In this case, the entire
 state can demonstrate higher or lower-than-average growth (e.g.,
 what is the value of a dollar today in 2018 terms?).

 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 9</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/11.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Baseline Referenced SGPs
• Instead of re-norming growth from year-to-year, it is possible to use growth-
 norms derived from a previous cohorts of students to calculate students’
 SGPs.
 • This approach has been utilized in Utah and more than a dozen other
 states to investigate COVID-19 impact/recovery (learning deceleration/
 acceleration).
 • Adequate growth percentiles can be calculated with respect to baseline
 growth norms.
 • Mean/Median SGPs can deviate from 50.
• Baseline SGPs can be calculated correcting for measurement error (SIMEX &amp;
 ranked SIMEX measurement error correction).
• Baseline SGPs can be calculated using previous “super-cohorts” of students.
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 11</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/12.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Baseline Referenced SGPs: Benefits
• Not a “zero sum game”. All students can demonstrate high
 growth.
• Allows for the detection of learning/growth acceleration
 and deceleration.
• Allows for the calculation of SGPs using preliminary data
 (don’t have to wait for entire cohort of data to be available).
• Unlike cohort-referenced SGPs, growth targets are NOT
 updated as new growth norms become available because
 growth norms remain fixed across years.
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 12</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/13.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Baseline Referenced SGPs: Requirements &amp; Detriments
• The use of baseline growth norms (to calculate baseline
 referenced SGPs) requires scale equivalence across years.
 • Scale drift will impact baseline SGP results.
 • As such, baseline SGPs can be a valuable asset in
 identifying scale drift (if growth acceleration is too good
 to be true, it probably is.)
• Depending upon how far the state goes in communicating
 details of the methodology, can be more complicated to
 explain than cohort referenced SGPs.
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 13</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/15.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Actual and Potential Uses of SGPs in Utah
1. Accountability: SGPs are the foundation of the “other
 academic indicator” and the “equity” indicator.
2. Monitoring: SGPs have been useful in understanding COVID
 impacts and rates of recovery. They can also be used to
 monitor local educational programs.
3. Evaluation: SGPs (or other student growth measures) can
 support more defensible causal conclusions than changes in
 proficiency when evaluating programs, curriculum, or
 strategies.
4. Warning: Low SGPs are a red flag warning for students,
 especially for low-achieving students.
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 15</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/16.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">How Do SGPs Work in Accountability?
• There are several ways that SGPs and AGPs can be used in
 accountability.
• Utah has used both AGPs (SGTs) and SGPs in accountability for
 many years.
• In April 2022, the U.S. Department of Education approved
 Utah’s 2022 addendum, which proposed indexing points for
 growth based on SGP only, as shown on the following slide.

 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 16</div>
```

The total number of points across all students is divided by the number of tests. This

growth) to arrive at the growth points for each school.
This represents about 1/3 of the total accountability weight for 3-8 schools.

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/20.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">What We’re Learning From Growth Results

 Rates of learning, on average, are slightly exceeding or at pre-
 pandemic rates of growth. The SYSTEM has recovered, and then
 some.

 Student attainment, on average, is still lagging because rates of
 learning have not accelerated enough to catch students up. In
 other words, students have not fully “recovered,” but their levels
 are, in most grades, close to pre-pandemic levels.

 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 20</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/21.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Growth as an Evaluation Metric
• Using student longitudinal growth measures in evaluation
 studies avoids several of these pitfalls.
• Students serve as their own “control group.” If the growth
 trajectories change noticeably, we can posit that the program
 or policy had an effect.
• We recently evaluated a state’s accountability system. One of
 the key questions was whether being identified for CSI had an
 effect on the school’s outcomes.
 ▪ Aggregate measures of student growth are an important outcome
 and leading indicator.
 ▪ In other words, increases in proficiency should follow increases in
 growth.
 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 21</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/25.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Revisiting the UAAD Claims and Responses
• Immediate Results:
 ▪ The baseline results can be produced faster than the cohort-
 referenced SGPS, especially with preliminary data.
• Stable and Consistent Comparison:
 ▪ Yes, as long as the test scale remains stable, baseline-referenced
 SGPs are useful for monitoring trends
• Enhanced Utility for Planning:
 ▪ This assumption is based on the immediate delivery of results.
 The enhanced utility is still an open question.

 Utah Growth Model Discussion (5/19/25) 25</div>
```
